interpretation: The frozen primary positive association is directionally consistent and leave-one-clade-out stable, but it does not meet the predeclared two-sided permutation threshold (P=0.06147). It is therefore not supported. The result is compatible with a link between overall fine-colour persistence and hidden-memory realization, but the current 21-clade analysis does not establish that link.
biological_implication: Global exact-colour persistence and hierarchical within-coarse organization are not interchangeable measures. Their point association is moderately positive, while fine-minus-coarse persistence advantage is essentially unrelated to hidden memory. A future independent test can target the specific prediction that radiations with stronger absolute fine-colour persistence tend to preserve more hidden within-coarse lineage structure.
claim_boundary: primary decision remains NOT SUPPORTED because frozen two-sided permutation P exceeds 0.05
do not reinterpret the directional expectation as permission for a post-outcome one-sided test
bootstrap and leave-one-out stability are robustness descriptors, not a rescue
secondary relations cannot replace the frozen primary
shared source states and phylogenies mean this is not independent replication
relative divergence depth only; no absolute-time claim
no ecological or molecular cause inferred
next_gate: If this temporal-realization relation is tested again, freeze the positive fine-persistence prediction in an independent radiation set or future source before opening hidden-memory outcomes; do not tune the current 21-clade threshold or predictor.
